record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: Can the high-accuracy orthogonal-polynomial-based sampling method for invariant unitary ensembles be extended to orthogonal and symplectic invariant ensembles?

evidence.quote: It is an open problem to extend the method of S. Olver et al. to orthogonal and symplectic invariant ensembles.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. For a unitary-invariant matrix ensemble on N×N Hermitian matrices with joint eigenvalue density proportional to
   ∏_{i<j}(x_i−x_j)^2 · ∏_i w(x_i),
the eigenvalues form a determinantal point process whose correlation kernel is
   K_N(x,y) = √{w(x)w(y)} · Σ_{k=0}^{N−1} p_k(x) p_k(y),
where {p_k} are the orthonormal polynomials associated with the weight w. Using this representation, exact sampling of the eigenvalues can be performed to high accuracy via the algorithm: draw x_1 from the marginal density K_N(x,x)/N, then sequentially draw x_{j+1} from the conditional density obtained by Schur-complementing the kernel against the previously sampled points. This requires only the ability to compute the orthonormal polynomials p_k for the weight w with sufficient accuracy.

The orthogonal (β=1) and symplectic (β=4) invariant ensembles have joint eigenvalue densities proportional to
   ∏_{i<j}|x_i−x_j|^β · ∏_i w(x_i),  β ∈ {1,4},
and form Pfaffian point processes with 2×2 matrix-valued skew-symmetric correlation kernels expressible in terms of the skew-orthogonal polynomials associated with w.

Problem. Develop an exact, high-accuracy sampling algorithm for the eigenvalues of the orthogonal (β=1) and symplectic (β=4) invariant ensembles with a general weight function w, analogous to the orthogonal-polynomial-based algorithm available for the unitary (β=2) case. In particular, provide (i) an effective numerical method for computing the skew-orthogonal polynomials associated with w, and (ii) a sequential conditional-sampling procedure based on the resulting 2×2 matrix-valued Pfaffian kernel, that produces samples from the joint eigenvalue distribution to a prescribed accuracy.
artifact.status_search_result: A recent preprint, "Sampling Pfaffian point processes and the symplectic Arnoldi method" (arXiv:2605.01202), presents an exact sampling algorithm for Pfaffian point processes—based on a skew-symmetric analogue of Cholesky factorization—together with a symplectic Arnoldi method for computing the skew-orthogonal polynomials needed to build the 2×2 matrix-valued kernels of β=1,4 ensembles. Numerical examples include the finite-N Gaussian orthogonal and symplectic ensembles and the β=1,4 Airy/Tracy–Widom distributions, indicating that the extension of the orthogonal-polynomial-based sampling method to orthogonal and symplectic invariant ensembles has been carried out.

status_evidence.title: Sampling Pfaffian point processes and the symplectic Arnoldi method
status_evidence.snippet: An exact sampling algorithm for Pfaffian point processes... enables sampling eigenvalues of the orthogonal and symplectic ensembles (β = 1,4)... a symplectic Arnoldi method for computing skew-orthogonal polynomials...
status_evidence.claim: Provides an exact sampling algorithm for β=1 and β=4 invariant ensembles via skew-orthogonal polynomials, extending the Olver–Nadakuditi–Trogdon unitary-ensemble method.

status_evidence.title: Sampling unitary invariant ensembles (arXiv:1404.0071)
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm for sampling unitary invariant ensembles based on orthogonal polynomials and the determinantal kernel.
status_evidence.claim: This is the β=2 method that the open problem asks to extend to β=1,4.
